![Project Banner](assets/banner.png) # Customer Uplift Modeling & Causal Machine Learning ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.11-3776AB?style=flat-square&logo=python&logoColor=white) ![Scikit-Learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-F7931E?style=flat-square&logo=scikit-learn&logoColor=white) ![LightGBM](https://img.shields.io/badge/LightGBM-2E7D32?style=flat-square&logo=lightgbm&logoColor=white) ![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green?style=flat-square)

Individual Treatment Effect (ITE) estimation, Two-Model Meta-Learners, Qini curve evaluation, and promotional budget optimization for e-commerce campaigns.

--- ## Overview Traditional predictive machine learning models estimate conditional conversion probability $P(Y \mid X)$, identifying which customers are likely to purchase. In promotional marketing, this creates substantial budgetary waste by subsidizing customers who would have purchased regardless of whether an incentive was issued. Causal Uplift Modeling shifts the objective from predicting conversion to estimating the **Individual Treatment Effect (ITE)** under the Rubin Potential Outcomes framework: $$\tau(X_i) = \mathbb{E}[Y_i(1) - Y_i(0) \mid X_i]$$ Where: - $Y_i(1)$: Potential conversion outcome if customer $i$ receives a promotional incentive ($T=1$) - $Y_i(0)$: Potential conversion outcome if customer $i$ is held in the control group ($T=0$) - $\tau(X_i)$: Individual Treatment Effect (Uplift / CATE) ### The Four Customer Response Archetypes Every customer cohort is partitioned into four behavioral archetypes: 1. **Persuadables ($\tau \gg 0$):** Convert only when receiving a promotional incentive. This is the sole target segment that generates net positive return on marketing spend. 2. **Sure Things ($Y(1)=1, Y(0)=1, \tau \approx 0$):** Purchase unconditionally. Issuing discounts to this segment erodes gross margin without generating incremental volume. 3. **Lost Causes ($Y(1)=0, Y(0)=0, \tau \approx 0$):** Never convert regardless of promotional incentives. Targeting them wastes marketing capital. 4. **Sleeping Dogs ($\tau < 0$):** Negatively affected by marketing touchpoints (unsubscribing or churning due to promotional contact). Marketing must strictly be suppressed. --- ## Architecture & Methodology
![Pipeline Architecture](assets/pipeline-architecture.png)
The pipeline executes through sequential modules: 1. **A/B Randomized Cohort Ingestion:** Ingests 30,000 randomized controlled trial customer interaction records. 2. **Covariate Transformation:** Encodes categorical platform features and standardizes continuous engagement metrics while sequestering treatment labels. 3. **Dual Meta-Learner Formulation:** Trains independent LightGBM estimators for control ($\mu_0$) and treated ($\mu_1$) customer arms to eliminate treatment regularization bias. 4. **Causal Evaluation (Qini Curves):** Evaluates ranking performance against unobservable counterfactuals via cumulative uplift curves. 5. **Budget Frontier Optimization:** Formulates gross margin vs incentive unit cost to locate the exact cutoff decile that maximizes net incremental revenue. 6. **Inference Interface:** Generates real-time individual uplift scores, customer archetypes, and binary promotional allocation decisions. --- ## Dataset & A/B Trial Cohort The dataset comprises 30,000 customer records collected during an A/B promotional trial with a balanced 50% treatment and 50% control assignment. | Feature Attribute | Data Type | Domain Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | recency_days | Integer | Days elapsed since previous completed purchase | | history_spend | Float | Cumulative monetary spend over trailing 12 months ($) | | visit_frequency | Integer | Number of active app sessions over trailing 30 days | | browse_duration_mins | Float | Mean session browsing engagement time (minutes) | | discount_sensitivity_score | Float | Normalized historical promotion usage ratio (0.0 to 1.0) | | preferred_device | Categorical | Primary access platform (Mobile App, Desktop Web, Mobile Web) | | membership_tier | Categorical | Loyalty program status (Standard, Silver, Gold, Platinum) | | channel_source | Categorical | User acquisition source (Organic, Social Media, Paid Search, Referral) | | treatment | Binary Indicator | A/B allocation: 0 = Control (No Incentive), 1 = Treatment (Promotional Voucher) | | conversion | Binary Target | Campaign conversion outcome: 1 = Purchased within 14 days, 0 = Did not purchase | --- ## Customer Archetype Segmentation Plotting estimated individual treatment effects ($\tau$) against baseline conversion propensity ($P(Y=1 \mid T=0)$) establishes operational boundaries for customer segmentation.
![Customer Uplift Segmentation Matrix](assets/uplift-segmentation-matrix.png)
### Key Archetype Takeaways - **Persuadables Cohort:** Located in the upper-left quadrant (low baseline propensity, high positive uplift). These users represent the highest priority for incentive allocation. - **Sure Things Cohort:** Concentrated in the upper-right region (high baseline conversion >20%). Suppressing promotions in this segment protects baseline revenue margins. - **Negative Lift Region:** Identifies marginal users sensitive to notification fatigue, providing actionable suppression boundaries. --- ## Meta-Learner Benchmarking (Qini Curve Analysis) Because counterfactual outcomes for individual users cannot be observed directly, standard predictive metrics like ROC-AUC or MSE cannot evaluate uplift models. Causal models are evaluated through cumulative uplift and Qini curves.
![Qini Curve Benchmark](assets/qini-curve-benchmark.png)
### Quantitative Ranking Benchmarks | Meta-Learner Architecture | Underlying Estimator | Qini Score (AUUC Gain) | Causal Evaluation Assessment | | :--- | :--- | :---: | :--- | | Random Targeting Baseline | Stochastic Assignment | 0.00 | Uniform baseline with zero ranking efficiency | | T-Learner Pipeline | Dual LightGBM Classifiers | 32.96 | Robust isolation of treatment effect across cohorts | | S-Learner Architecture | Single LightGBM Classifier | 35.26 | Joint covariate modeling with treatment feature interaction | The Qini metric measures cumulative incremental conversions achieved per percentage of population targeted, ordered from highest predicted uplift to lowest. Both meta-learners exhibit substantial separation above random allocation across all deciles. --- ## Marketing Budget Optimization & ROI Frontier A standard marketing campaign often blasts promotions to the entire customer base (100% targeting). Under realistic unit economics: $$\text{Gross Margin per Conversion} = \$40.00$$ $$\text{Promotional Incentive Cost} = \$7.00 \quad (\text{Discount value and operational cost})$$ The Net Incremental Profit function across population percentiles ($k$) is formalized as: $$\text{Net Incremental Profit}(k) = \text{Targeted Users}(k) \times \left( \Delta p(k) \times \$40.00 - \$7.00 \right)$$ Where $\Delta p(k)$ represents the empirical lift rate in the top $k$ percent of the population.
![Marketing Budget Optimization](assets/incremental-roi-frontier.png)
### Financial Performance Comparison | Campaign Targeting Strategy | Targeted Population Cutoff | Net Incremental Profit | Economic Impact | | :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- | | Naive Blast-All Campaign | Top 100% of Base | -$6,423.83 | Substantial loss due to incentive subsidy on non-responsive cohorts | | **Causal Uplift Optimal Policy** | **Top 52.0% of Base** | **+$2,426.17** | **+$8,850.00 Net Economic Value Preserved vs Blast-All** | Restricting marketing incentives to the top 52.0% of customers maximizes net incremental campaign profit, turning an otherwise loss-making marketing blast into a profitable campaign. --- ## Treatment Heterogeneity & Feature Drivers
![Uplift Distribution by Tier](assets/uplift-distribution-by-tier.png)
![Feature Causal Importance](assets/feature-causal-importance.png)
- **Discount Sensitivity:** The dominant feature dictating individual treatment effect magnitude. Customers with high historical coupon affinity exhibit the steepest lift response. - **Engagement Duration:** Extended browsing duration signals active consideration, magnifying responsiveness to conversion incentives. - **Membership Tier Heterogeneity:** Silver and Gold tiers exhibit the highest variance in lift response, representing prime candidates for personalized incentive amounts. --- ## License MIT: [LICENSE](LICENSE)
